sections.text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: So be it, My beloved friend! I will unfold to thee some of the chief aspects of My glory. Of its full extent there is no end.
O Arjuna! I am the Self, seated in the hearts of all beings; I am the beginning and the life, and I am the end of them all.
Of all the creative Powers I am the Creator, of luminaries the Sun; the Whirlwind among the winds, and the Moon among planets.

We had been discussing Chapter 10, Vibhuti yoga, Yoga of Divine Glories. So far, up to chapters one through nine, we came to one conclusion: that everything comes out of one single entity and everything is pervaded by him. Over and over Bhagavan said that you should focus on that entity which is permanent, that which never changes.
Along with all the changes happening in this Sansar, everything is constantly changing , including my body, my mind, my intellect. But theyre part of the prakriti. But as long as you identify with this unchanging reality which is all pervading and the source of all the beings, then thou shall be liberated from all your sorrows and limitations.
So Arjuna, like all of us, says that I intellectually appreciate this. Many, many Rishis have said this, and now you are also telling me the same thing. But how do I contemplate upon that single entity is still not clear to me.
Intellectually appreciating that he is everywhere is one thing, and when encounter a situation which is unconducive, to keep that thought steady in your mind is another thing. And thats why Arjuna said I am having difficulty. I cannot conceptualize in my mind what is that all pervading entity is all about.
You need to give me some pointers. Something which I can tangibly can relate to, which I can conceptualize in my mind, in my meditation, in my contemplation, where I can hang on to that entity as the divine entity, as the one all pervading entity. And then I may make some progress.
So tell me all your glories without leaving anything behind, because I never get tired of listening to it. You tell me all these times. So tell me what is it that I should be looking for in this universe which I can identify as your manifestation? Everything I see right now, even though I have understood, come very short of being divine.
So what should I focus on? So in response to that, we have this next 22 verses which Bhagavan gives Various pointers to meditate upon. It is not very clear to us how to identify divinity. So Bhagavan said, you find divinity in everything that is best among their own spheres.
So Bhagavan starts his response by clarifying that we are not coming to any new conclusion now , that only the best is where I am, but not the rest. Verse 20 clearly makes a summary statement: lets not get deviated from what we already talked about, that I am the source of all the beings, Asheshena, without leaving anything out. But in some, this divinity may be more prominent to identify.
So he says: Aham Atma Gudakesha Sarva Bhuta Ashayasthitah. Lets make it clear that I reside as the core of all the beings. There is no exception.
Just because we say the one is more manifesting divinity and other is not, that does not mean the other is devoid of my presence. So very first clarification is I reside in all the beings as the core of their beings. Aham adhisha madhyacha bhutanam anta evacha.
I am the origin, Adi middle and the end of all the beings. All the beings are part of the Prakriti. They have beginning and end.
They come from somewhere. They exist in time and space for a while and then they end. But all the time the source of that being is me.
I am the one who sustained them during their existence. And I am the one they dissolve into. That you should never forget, Bhagavanji, even in your contemplation, that there is no exception.
There is nothing which can exist without my presence. But your question was: what to contemplate upon? How can I conceptualize the divinity, the self, which is all pervading and immortal? So Ill give you the pointers. In the next 21 verses Bhagawan gave 75 pointers.
It is like something obvious we can identify with. When the lights are on in this room, we know the electricity is there. When lights were off, electricity was still here.
It just was not available for my perception. The electricity always pervades in this room in all this electrical wiring. I can only prove when I show you the presence of it in some manifest form.
So the manifest forms rest of the chapter talks about. And because it is given to Arjuna in his time, we obviously walk through several of these Vedic and Puranic references. If Krishna were talking today, he would say, I am the iPhone among all smartphones.
Im Google among all technology companies. We relate to things which are familiar to us, and therefore the analogies given are more in line with the culture at the time. And what Arjuna can identify with , he starts out from the higher, then comes down to the level which in day-to-day life Arjuna can identify with. Adityanam Aham Vishnuh , among the Adityas, I am Vishnu.
Aditis sons are the Adityas. Aditi is mentioned in the Rig Veda. Aditi means limitless.
Aditi is the mother of all celestial beings. Later, in Puranic time, Aditi was also shown as wife of Kashyap Rishi. But from the Vedic point of view, Aditi was the perennial mother, the primordial mother who gives birth to this universe.
According to our scriptures and puranas, sometimes four Adityas are mentioned, sometimes six. But eventually they settled on 12 Adityas. When the word is used in the singular, it means Sun.
When mentioned in the plural, it means the 12. The Adityas somewhat identify with the 12 months of the year; each one is in charge of one segment of the year. So among the Adityas, Bhagavan says I am Vishnu.
Vishnu is all pervading. Vishnu means one who has long reach. You can probably say that the one in charge of the longest day in the year is Vishnu.
But basically, among all the celestial beings, what becomes very apparent to me is Vishnu because he is all pervading. Consider me as Vishnu among all Adityas. Jyotisham Ravihi Anshuman , among the luminaries in the sky, those objects or entities that are self-effulgent, I am the radiant Sun.
Sun is something obvious to us. But we can only relate to Sun. Among the luminaries in the sky, I am Sun.
Marichihi Marutam Asmi among the winds, wind is air in different forms. It can be hurricane, it can be tornado, it can be storm or it can be a pleasant breeze. Marutas in plurality are in charge of all these different types of winds.
Now obviously in Vedic time, we were reliant on the natural forces. Natural forces are something we are trying to understand. So each natural force is a deity.
We came to one conclusion that if there is an activity, there is somebody in charge of the activity. Activity cannot take place unless there is somebody guiding it. If I see an effect, there has to be a cause.
If I see a wind moving, there is A cause somebody is in charge. Somebody making sure that in this condition only this thing can occur. So marutas were in charge of winds.
And each type of wind has a different maruta. The Marichi is among the best because it is the in charge of the pleasant breeze which we can enjoy. We are afraid of tornado, we are afraid of hurricane.
But we are very happy when this pleasant breeze is flowing. Among all the Marutas, Nakshatranam, Ahamshashi, Nakshatrana, the asterisms or constellations among them all the arrangement of stars in the sky. In Nakshatra, the moon appears to be traveling through these star clusters.
So when I see the night sky, the asterisms are dimly lit, but the moon is brightly lit. He seems like the king of all these asterisms, traveling through all these Nakshatras as if he were the king of all the Nakshatras. So therefore he says, among the Nakshatras, I am Shashi.
He say, consider me as the sun. Night time I see moon. He says, consider me as moon.
If it is windy, consider that my Maruta are working. But when you feel at ease, most at comfort, I am Marichi. And among all the celestial beings, I am Vishnu.
Without Vishnu, nothing can exist. So therefore, when you see anything, something which catches your imagination, something that can invoke these divine feelings in you, consider that my presence you are experiencing. The next verse says Vedanam Sama Vedo Asmi.
Obviously, Arjuna was a product of a Vedic culture. We consider Vedas the basis of our culture. If things cannot have a proof in Vedas, it is not true.
Truth has to have basis in Vedas. And obviously we know there are four Vedas. Rug Veda, Sam Veda, Yajurveda and Tharva Veda.
Sam Veda is most pleasant. Saam Veda is basically as we have heard all in poetry. Rug Veda is in prose, Sama Veda in poetry.
So listening to Sama Veda is most pleasant. Even today if you listen to our Panditji, he is Samavedi. When he chant, it really catches your attention.
Chanting normally going on in temple, everybody is talking. You know, when he starts in a Sam Vedi chanting, everybody is quiet. Something really unique, something which catches your attention, something which catches your mind is Sama Veda.
Among all the Vedas, I am Sama Veda. Knowledge is in all Vedas. But something that can invoke the sense of divinity in your heart is when you have this beautiful Poetry sung in a proper raga.
So if a Vedas discussion is going on and it is not interesting to me, its like the Ghata Pata. You know, theres two pandits talking about this Vedic discussion. They give examples: Ghata and Pata, Ghata and Pata.
One who cannot get anything out of it says, All this is Garbhat , they are doing Garbhat. Thats where the word Garbhat comes from. Because we cannot understand what they are talking about.
So its Garbhat to us, even though they may be talking at the highest level. But even one who has no knowledge of Veda , if he listens to the Sama Veda, he will have that divinity experience in his heart. Bharu Bhagavan said, among Vedas, I am Sama Veda Devanam Asmi, Vasavah, Vasava Indra.
Among the Devas, I am Indra. We know Indra is the king of all the Devas. He is the mightiest, he is the wealthiest.
He is the greatest kingdom Splendor. Deva Loka is supposed to be a place for enjoyment. Even the Devas have all these politics among themselves.
Who is higher, who is lower. They have as much jealousy as us. This is serial Kantosima.
Indras wife Paulami is the bad one and Santosima is the good one. One harasses people and one tries to save people. So among Devas, in other words, even if you reach to a level of goodness, your shortcomings will still be there.
If I want to be happy and say, if I become a millionaire or a billionaire, Ill be happy. All your shortcomings will be with you when you become billionaire. What is making me unhappy will make me unhappy.
Then also just having wealth, just having accomplishment is not a remedy for any happiness or experiencing any divinity. But even when you consider that as the basis of divinity, I am among all Devasam Indra, most accomplished, the king of all. From a material wealth perspective, Indriyana Manasthyasmi.
Even in the previous line, he also said among the Devasam Indra Deva means to Dev is to illuminate. That which illuminates is the Deva.

Krishna begins His enumeration with a crucial clarification: Aham Atma Gudakesha sarva-bhutashaya-sthitah - I am the Self dwelling in the hearts of all beings. Before listing specific glories, He establishes the universal foundation: divinity is not only in the excellent but in all. He is the beginning, middle, and end of all beings - their source, sustenance, and dissolution. This prevents a common misunderstanding: that only special, excellent things are divine while ordinary things are not.
Then come the celestial manifestations: among the Adityas (sun-deities), He is Vishnu the all-pervading; among luminaries, the radiant Sun; among the Maruts (wind-gods), He is Marichi the gentle breeze; among the Nakshatras (stars), He is the Moon. Notice the principle: in each category, Krishna identifies with what is most prominent, most beneficial, most capable of evoking awe. When you look up at the sun, you are seeing divine glory. When a pleasant breeze refreshes you, that is Marichi - divine comfort made tangible.
Today, practice this cosmic vision. When you see sunlight streaming through a window, recognize it as Krishnas glory. When wind touches your face, feel the divine presence. The examples may seem archaic - we no longer worship the Adityas - but the principle is timeless. In whatever catches your attention and evokes wonder, the divine is more visibly present. What are the Suns and Moons in your life - those things that illuminate, that you cannot help but notice? Can you begin to see them as pointers to their source rather than ends in themselves?
